name: Pale-legged Leaf Warbler
rangeDescription: Breeds river valleys of northeastern asia; winters in southeastern asia
description: Small songbird, dull brownish-olive above, pale below, with prominent white supercilium, black eyeline, and faint, narrow wingbars. Vertical tail pumping distinguishes this species from most others in its range except Sakhalin Leaf Warbler.

name: Gray-crested Finch
rangeDescription: Arid andes of southeastern bolivia and northwestern argentina (jujuy and salta)
description: Small, mostly terrestrial finch-like tanager of dry intermontane valleys from central Bolivia to NW Argentina. Plain gray plumage and erect crest distinctive.

name: Steel-blue Whydah
rangeDescription: Southern south sudan, ethiopia, somalia, northern uganda, kenya, and northern and central tanzania
description: A nest parasite that lays its eggs in the nests of Black-cheeked and Black-faced Waxbills. As with other whydahs, breeding males are distinctive, whereas non-breeding males and females are drab and inconspicuous.

name: Tawny-browed Owl
rangeDescription: Eastern paraguay to southeastern brazil and northeastern argentina (misiones)
description: Large brown owl with dark eyes and distinctive white semicircles on its face. Streaked below with distinctive pale white bars.

name: Friendly Bush Warbler
rangeDescription: Montane forest of northern borneo (mounts kinabalu and trus madi)
description: Though frequently derided for the reputed inaccuracy of its name, this mouse-like bird can prove quite confiding. It is, however, generally quite difficult to see in dense undergrowth; best detected by its song, a series of three piercing whistles, the last of which is long and grating.

name: Magpie Starling
rangeDescription: Sudan to southern ethiopia, somalia, northeastern uganda, kenya, and tanzania
description: An unusual and distinctive starling of dry country. Males are dark above and white below, with a blue-black hood and upperparts; females are dark gray.

name: Rufous-headed Pygmy-Tyrant
rangeDescription: Andes of colombia to western bolivia (la paz and cochabamba)
description: Tiny, plump flycatcher found in the understory of subtropical and temperate cloud forest in the Andes. Not likely to be confused.

name: Rufous-bellied Bush-Tyrant
rangeDescription: East slope of andes of southern peru (pasco) to western bolivia
description: Subtly patterned reddish-brown flycatcher of high-elevation montane forests. Perches upright, often on the tops of snags or bushes around forest edges and clearings.

name: Volcano Swiftlet
rangeDescription: Mountains of java
description: A Javan endemic, this rare and enigmatic swiftlet breeds in the craters of a handful of active volcanoes. Forages over the craters and surrounding montane forest.

name: Scarlet-shouldered Parrotlet
rangeDescription: Patchily distributed northern south america to northern bolivia and northern brazil
description: Small parrot, widespread but uncommon across the lowlands of northern South America. Difficult to see well unless a flock drops into a clay lick; otherwise, most often detected by voice as they pass over in high-flying flocks.

name: Huayco Tinamou
rangeDescription: Andes of northwestern bolivia to northwestern argentina
description: Large, streaky tinamou of upper elevations of the east side of the Andes. The highland version of Red-winged Tinamou, similar in voice and habits.

name: Striated Lorikeet
rangeDescription: Mountains of western new guinea (snow mountains to chimbu province)
description: A rare, medium-sized lorikeet of foothill and lower montane forest. Green body with yellow-green striations on the face and underparts, and a gray band from the eye around the back of the head.

name: Socorro Dove
rangeDescription: Formerly socorro island (off western mexico); extinct in the wild since 1950s but a small captive population exists
description: Slender dove native to Socorro Island, located in the Pacific Ocean 360 miles from mainland Mexico. It was wiped out due to introduced feral cats and habitat loss, and last seen there in the seventies.

name: Bateleur
rangeDescription: Savanna and thornscrub of sub-saharan africa
description: A very distinctive, short-tailed eagle. Young birds are uniformly dark brown, and adults are mostly black with a bright red face and legs.

name: Forest Wagtail
rangeDescription: Russian far east to southeastern china and southern japan; winters to southern and southeastern asia
description: A distinctive wagtail with diagnostic wing and breast patterns. It has a prominent, whitish eyebrow with two black crescent-shaped bands on the upper breast; lower one wider when present.

name: Rufous Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Arid coastal northwestern peru (tumbes to northern lima)
description: Large flycatcher restricted to dry lowland forest in northwestern Peru, especially in areas with abundant mesquite and acacia. Well named; no other flycatcher in range is similarly colored.

name: Palawan Hornbill
rangeDescription: Southwestern philippines (palawan, balabac, busuanga, and calauit)
description: A large bird of lowland and foothill forest on Palawan and neighbouring islands. Entirely black except for a white tail and a long, thick, pale cream-colored bill and casque.

name: Masked Finfoot
rangeDescription: Bangladesh and northeastern india to indochina; winters to sumatra
description: A bizarre bird that loosely resembles a cormorant with a hornbill’s brightly-colored beak. Gray-brown overall with a black mask extending from the face down to the throat that is darker and more extensive in males.

name: Humboldt Penguin
rangeDescription: Humboldt current region of coastal northern peru to southern chile
description: Uncommon and local; breeds in colonies along the coast of Peru and Chile, where it nests in underground burrows. The only penguin in most of its range, but some overlap in central Chile with similar Magellanic Penguin of colder southern waters.

name: Sokoke Pipit
rangeDescription: Coastal forest of southeastern kenya and northeastern tanzania
description: A rare small pipit found in a limited region of the East African coast, where it is very local in coastal forest. Rich rufous-brown above and white below with bold streaking on the breast.
